claim: Patient's fasting blood glucose was 126 mg/dL on two separate occasions.
evidence: Lab results dated 03/15 and 03/22: fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL and 128 mg/dL respectively. Patient was confirmed fasting for at least 8 hours prior to each draw.
note: Direct numeric match across two measurements; classic diabetes diagnosis threshold test.

claim: Serum potassium level was within normal range at the time of discharge.
evidence: Discharge labs (03/28): Na 138 mEq/L, K 2.9 mEq/L, Cl 101 mEq/L, CO2 24 mEq/L. Patient was on furosemide 40 mg daily throughout admission.
note: K of 2.9 is below normal range (3.5–5.0 mEq/L); claim of 'within normal range' is directly contradicted.

claim: The patient's hemoglobin A1c level suggests long-term hyperglycemia.
evidence: CBC and metabolic panel drawn on admission. HbA1c not ordered during this encounter. Previous outpatient records not available for review.
note: No HbA1c data present; claim cannot be supported or refuted from available evidence.

claim: Serum creatinine is elevated, indicating possible acute kidney injury.
evidence: Renal function panel: BUN 42 mg/dL, creatinine 2.3 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL per prior records), eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73m². Clinical team initiated IV fluid resuscitation.
note: Creatinine >1.5× baseline meets KDIGO AKI criteria; claim is well-supported by numeric evidence.

claim: Troponin I levels remained undetectable throughout the hospitalization.
evidence: Serial troponin I: Admission 0.02 ng/mL (normal <0.04), 6 h 0.09 ng/mL (elevated), 12 h 0.15 ng/mL (elevated). Cardiology consulted for rising troponin trend.
note: Troponin rose to 0.09 and 0.15, contradicting the claim of undetectable levels.

claim: Complete blood count showed findings consistent with bacterial infection.
evidence: CBC: WBC 14.2 × 10³/μL with 82% neutrophils and bandemia of 11%. Hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, platelets 310 × 10³/μL.
note: Leukocytosis with left shift (bandemia) is a classic CBC pattern consistent with bacterial infection.

claim: Patient was started on vancomycin for coverage of MRSA.
evidence: Medication administration record: vancomycin 1250 mg IV q12h initiated on hospital day 2 per infectious disease recommendations for suspected MRSA bacteremia. Trough levels monitored per protocol.
note: Directly stated in MAR with indication documented; straightforward support case.

claim: The patient received aspirin 325 mg daily for antiplatelet therapy.
evidence: Current medication list on admission: aspirin 81 mg PO daily (home medication, continued), metformin 500 mg PO BID, lisinopril 10 mg PO daily.
note: Aspirin dose is 81 mg, not 325 mg; dose discrepancy directly contradicts the claim.

claim: Anticoagulation with warfarin was contraindicated due to recent intracranial hemorrhage.
evidence: Hematology note: patient has prior history of deep vein thrombosis managed with compression stockings. No anticoagulation initiated. Prior imaging reports not available in current electronic record.
note: No documentation of ICH in available evidence; contraindication claim cannot be verified.

claim: Patient was prescribed a beta-blocker as part of heart failure management.
evidence: Cardiology discharge summary: carvedilol 3.125 mg PO BID initiated for newly diagnosed HFrEF (EF 35%). Patient counseled on gradual titration schedule. ACE inhibitor and loop diuretic also prescribed.
note: Carvedilol is a beta-blocker explicitly prescribed for heart failure; claim is supported.

claim: Insulin therapy was discontinued upon discharge.
evidence: Discharge medication reconciliation: insulin glargine 20 units subcutaneous at bedtime — CONTINUE. Sliding scale regular insulin — CONTINUE. Metformin 1000 mg PO BID — NEW. Patient instructed on home glucose monitoring.
note: Insulin therapy was continued, not discontinued; directly contradicts the claim.

claim: No antibiotic therapy was administered during the hospitalization.
evidence: Physician orders and MAR reviewed. No antibiotic agents listed. Patient admitted for elective orthopedic procedure; infection prophylaxis not indicated per surgical protocol. IV access maintained for pain management only.
note: MAR confirms absence of antibiotics; claim of no antibiotic therapy is supported.

claim: The patient was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus during this admission.
evidence: Endocrinology consultation note: fasting glucose 136 mg/dL, HbA1c 8.2%. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus confirmed. Lifestyle counseling provided. Metformin initiated. Follow-up with outpatient endocrinologist in 4 weeks.
note: New T2DM diagnosis explicitly documented by specialist during the admission.

claim: Imaging confirmed the presence of a pulmonary embolism.
evidence: CT pulmonary angiography report: no filling defect identified in pulmonary vasculature. Bilateral lower lobe atelectasis noted. Heart size normal. D-dimer was mildly elevated at 0.6 μg/mL FEU.
note: CTPA explicitly negative for PE; elevated D-dimer alone does not confirm PE, claim contradicted.

claim: Differential diagnosis included community-acquired pneumonia.
evidence: Emergency department note: patient presented with 3-day history of productive cough, fever, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Chest X-ray and CBC ordered. Broad differential being considered pending results.
note: Clinical picture is consistent with CAP but it is not explicitly listed in a differential; insufficient to support.

claim: The patient carries a confirmed diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
evidence: Pulmonology note references prior spirometry (performed at outside facility): FEV1/FVC ratio 0.62 post-bronchodilator, FEV1 68% predicted. COPD diagnosed per GOLD criteria. Patient on tiotropium and albuterol PRN at home.
note: Spirometry-confirmed COPD with documented treatment; supports the claim definitively.

claim: The working diagnosis of acute appendicitis was excluded by imaging.
evidence: Surgical consult note: abdominal CT with contrast demonstrated acute appendicitis with periappendiceal fat stranding. Patient taken to operating room for laparoscopic appendectomy. Pathology confirmed acute suppurative appendicitis.
note: CT confirmed appendicitis; claim that it was excluded is directly contradicted by imaging and pathology.

claim: Echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.
evidence: Transthoracic echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at 55–60%. Grade I diastolic dysfunction noted. Mild mitral regurgitation. No wall motion abnormalities identified.
note: EF 55–60% is in preserved range (≥50%); claim directly supported by echo findings.

claim: Patient's blood pressure was consistently within normal limits during the monitoring period.
evidence: Nursing vital signs documentation (every 4 hours over 48-hour monitoring period): systolic range 108–122 mmHg, diastolic range 68–78 mmHg. No hypertensive episodes recorded. No antihypertensive interventions required.
note: All BP readings within normal range over extended monitoring; unambiguous support.

claim: Oxygen saturation remained above 95% on room air throughout the stay.
evidence: Telemetry and nursing notes: SpO2 dropped to 88% on room air on hospital day 3, prompting initiation of supplemental oxygen at 2 L/min via nasal cannula. SpO2 improved to 96% on supplemental O2.
note: SpO2 dropped to 88%, requiring supplemental O2; contradicts claim of staying above 95% on room air.

claim: Resting heart rate was elevated above 100 bpm on initial assessment.
evidence: Triage vital signs: Temperature 37.4°C, HR 92 bpm, RR 16/min, BP 118/74 mmHg, SpO2 98% on room air. Patient appeared anxious but in no acute distress.
note: HR was 92 bpm, below the 100 bpm threshold for tachycardia; claim contradicted by documented vitals.

claim: Patient was febrile on admission with a temperature exceeding 38.3°C.
evidence: Admission vital signs at 14:32: temperature 39.1°C (oral), heart rate 108 bpm, blood pressure 102/64 mmHg, respiratory rate 22/min, SpO2 97% on 2 L O2 via NC. Patient was diaphoretic.
note: Temperature 39.1°C clearly exceeds 38.3°C threshold; fever on admission well-supported.

claim: Respiratory rate normalized to below 20 breaths per minute after treatment.
evidence: Post-treatment reassessment at 2 hours: RR documented as 24/min. Physician note: 'respiratory status improved subjectively, though tachypnea persists.' Patient still on supplemental oxygen.
note: RR remains 24/min (above 20); subjective improvement noted but objective data contradicts claim.

claim: The patient's weight was not documented at admission.
evidence: Nursing admission assessment: height 170 cm, weight 84.3 kg, BMI 29.2 kg/m². Nutritional risk screening completed. Dietary consult placed.
note: Weight explicitly documented at 84.3 kg; claim that it was not recorded is directly contradicted.

claim: Patient has a history of myocardial infarction.
evidence: Past medical history as documented in the admission H&P: hypertension (10 years), hyperlipidemia, osteoarthritis of bilateral knees. Social history: 20 pack-year smoking history, quit 5 years ago. No prior cardiac events documented.
note: PMH explicitly lists conditions but excludes MI; claim directly contradicted by documented history.

claim: The patient has a documented allergy to penicillin.
evidence: Allergy section of admission record: penicillin — reaction: rash (hives), severity: moderate. Documented by patient self-report and confirmed with prior pharmacy records. Allergy band applied.
note: Penicillin allergy explicitly documented with reaction type; claim directly and unambiguously supported.

claim: Patient underwent coronary artery bypass grafting within the past five years.
evidence: Surgical history: appendectomy (childhood), cholecystectomy (12 years prior), right hip arthroplasty (3 years prior). No cardiovascular surgical procedures noted. Family history significant for coronary artery disease.
note: Surgical history documented without CABG; claim contradicted by documented absence in surgical history.

claim: Patient has a family history of colon cancer.
evidence: Social and family history: patient lives alone, retired teacher, non-smoker, occasional alcohol use. Family history section: 'Patient unable to provide detailed family history due to being adopted.' No family history documented.
note: No family history available; claim cannot be supported or refuted from incomplete data.

claim: The patient has previously received bariatric surgery.
evidence: Nutrition consult note: patient reports a 60-pound weight loss over the past 2 years through dietary modification and exercise. No prior surgeries affecting gastrointestinal anatomy reported. Gastric emptying study may be considered.
note: Weight loss attributed to lifestyle changes; prior surgeries absence noted, contradicting bariatric surgery claim.

claim: Patient has a history of chronic kidney disease stage 3.
evidence: Problem list from longitudinal care record: chronic kidney disease stage 3a (eGFR 45–59 mL/min/1.73m², last confirmed 6 months ago), type 2 diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, anemia of chronic disease.
note: CKD stage 3 explicitly on problem list with eGFR range; claim fully supported with staging detail.
